document.abstract: The Committee on Progress, as it was known then, was one of the first committees formed soon after the Society was founded in 1916. The 1920 Report of the Committee on Progress, published in Transactions of the Society in May 1920, consisted of five pages and concerned itself mainly with the manufacture of arc lamp carbons, motion-picture theater projection booth equipment, and the development of gas-filled incandescent lamps for projection. The report has been published annually since those formative years.
